answer: I'd like to describe the build-up to my first trip abroad, because I don't think I have ever been so excited. An event I was intensely excited about was a long-planned holiday to Nepal, my first proper trip outside Bangladesh. It was last winter, and I was going with two close friends from university after we had been saving for almost a year. For weeks beforehand I was almost unable to think about anything else, and the [[anticipation]] was overwhelming. I spent hours researching places to visit and imagining what it would be like to see the Himalayas with my own eyes. Helping students travel abroad is my job, but this time it was finally my turn, which made it even more special. The night before departure I was so [[restless]] that I barely slept, and I checked my passport at least five times. My younger sister made me promise to bring her back a souvenir. When the day finally arrived and the plane took off, I felt a rush of pure [[exhilaration]]. The trip itself lived up to every expectation, filled with new sights, foods and experiences, especially the view of snow-capped mountains from Pokhara. What made the excitement so special was that it was building towards something I had dreamed about for years. Honestly, the joy of looking forward to it was almost as good as the trip itself. That experience taught me that anticipation is a wonderful part of any adventure. It remains one of the most [[unforgettable]] and genuinely [[thrilling]] experiences of my life.

followUps.q: Where would you like to travel next?
followUps.answer: I'd love to visit somewhere in Europe, perhaps the UK, since so many of my students go there. Ideally I would go as a student myself, which is something I really hope to do one day.
Very much. Reading about a place, choosing where to stay and making a rough plan is half the fun for me. My friends usually leave the planning to me, which I don't mind at all.

note: Made it a trip to Nepal with university friends, tied to his job; plain 'memorable' replaced by 'unforgettable', added 'thrilling'.
